independent_derivation: Let B be the finite bond carrier, beta:B->C the supplied boundary, and K_t^(s)[b,a]=K_t((s,b),a). The full stage has rows/columns indexed by {0,1} x B. Already emitted bits are spectators; a new highest wire is initialized to zero.

For a prefix p of length n and last bit s, expand the genuine matrix-vector action. The spectator identity eliminates every input prefix other than p, and the fresh-zero vector eliminates input bit 1. Thus R_(n+1)(p::s,b)=sum_a U_n((s,b),(0,a)) R_n(p,a). No global state-action equation has been assumed.
Define T_0(empty)=I_B and T_(n+1)(p::s)=K_n^(s) T_n(p). Hence T_n(x)=K_(n-1)^(x_(n-1)) ... K_0^(x_0), with later emission on the left. At n=0, R_0(empty,b)=beta_b=(I_B beta)_b.

Induct for every prefix and every intermediate bond label a, with beta fixed but arbitrary. Substituting clean-column equality and the induction hypothesis yields R_(n+1)(p::s,b)=sum_a K_n^(s)[b,a](T_n(p) beta)_a=(K_n^(s) T_n(p) beta)_b=(T_(n+1)(p::s) beta)_b. This proves all full-output amplitudes for every length.

At each used stage every input column (1,a) is irrelevant, for all a in B and all output rows. All input columns (0,a) remain covered by the premise; no blanket claim about unused clean bond columns follows without an additional support invariant. For a fixed length n, stages t>=n are not used at all. A different completion with identical clean columns gives the same run, even if its dirty-input columns differ.

independent_derivation: Put p_lambda=|c_lambda|^2 and S={lambda:c_lambda != 0}. Normalization ensures S is nonempty. Linearity of the retained-label controlled unitary gives Psi_tilde=sum_lambda c_lambda exp(i phi_lambda)|lambda> tensor psi_lambda. Both intended and actual vectors are unit vectors: cross-label inner products vanish even if the psi_lambda overlap.

For every real chi, orthonormality of label states and unit norms of branch outputs give ||Psi_tilde-exp(i chi)Psi||^2=sum_lambda p_lambda |exp(i phi_lambda)-exp(i chi)|^2=2-2 sum_lambda p_lambda cos(phi_lambda-chi)=4 sum_lambda p_lambda sin^2((phi_lambda-chi)/2). This is the requested exact full-output norm, with no phase quotient built into it.

A sum of nonnegative terms is zero exactly when every populated term vanishes. Exact equality Psi_tilde=Psi therefore holds iff exp(i phi_lambda)=1 for every lambda in S. Equality up to one common phase holds iff there is z of modulus one such that exp(i phi_lambda)=z for every lambda in S, equivalently phi_lambda-phi_mu is an integer multiple of 2 pi for all populated pairs. Phases of zero-coefficient labels are irrelevant.

Every isolated branch exp(i phi_lambda) psi_lambda has the same probabilities as psi_lambda for every measurement; this cannot detect phase differences between labels. For an explicit example use Lambda={0,1}, H=C^2, clean |0>, psi_0=psi_1=|0>, c_0=c_1=1/sqrt(2), V_0=I_2, V_1=-I_2, phi_0=0, phi_1=pi. These are unitary implementations and individually physically identical to the desired branch state. Intended Psi=|+> tensor |0>, actual Psi_tilde=|-> tensor |0>; their inner product is zero. Measuring the retained label in the {|+>,|->} basis gives opposite deterministic outcomes. Measuring in the original label basis would not distinguish them.

The mathematical correction is D=sum_lambda exp(-i phi_lambda)|lambda><lambda|. D is unitary and (D tensor I_H)Psi_tilde=Psi exactly. Arbitrary unit-modulus choices are allowed on unpopulated labels. The negative sign is required by the specified +i branch phase.

A single populated label is always correct up to a global phase, but exact equality still requires its phase factor to be 1. A common populated phase z gives Psi_tilde=z Psi and exact equality only if z=1. Known exact phase values suffice to specify D mathematically; a supplier, finite representation/precision analysis, gate synthesis, and resource charge for implementing D are separate obligations. Metadata alone does not apply D, and no work reset or cleanup is supplied beyond what is already present in each psi_lambda.

independent_derivation: Write B=2 eta, so 0<B<1, and C=sum_j c_j>0. The feasible domain has 0<delta_j<=1 and sum_j m_j delta_j<=B. Every feasible delta_j<=B/m_j<1, so every upper cap is redundant, not just inactive at the optimizer.

Define delta_j^*=B c_j/(C m_j). It is positive, strictly less than 1, and sum_j m_j delta_j^*=B. Its objective is T^*=sum_j c_j log_2(C m_j/(B c_j)). This establishes an explicit feasible candidate, including r=1.

For any feasible delta set t_j=delta_j/delta_j^*>0. Since m_j delta_j=(B/C)c_j t_j, sum_j c_j t_j<=C. Therefore (ln 2)(T(delta)-T^*)=-sum_j c_j ln t_j >= sum_j c_j(1-t_j)>=0 by ln t<=t-1. Equality in the first inequality, given every c_j>0, forces all t_j=1. Hence delta^* is the global unique minimizer; this is a sufficiency and uniqueness proof, not just stationary equations.

Let b_j^*=log_2(1/delta_j^*)>0 and choose b_j=ceil(b_j^*), a nonnegative integer. Then 2^(-b_j)<=delta_j^*, so the supplied multiplicity-weighted certificate yields ||V-U||<=(1/2)sum_j m_j 2^(-b_j)<=eta. Reuse is counted m_j times in error but once as c_j b_j in the assumed precision cost.

The rounded tolerance vector is feasible for the continuous problem and its objective equals sum_j c_j b_j, so T^*<=sum_j c_j b_j. Also b_j<b_j^*+1 for every j; finite positive weights give sum_j c_j b_j<T^*+C. No exact integer optimality follows. For example eta=1/8, m=(3,1), c=(2,1) gives delta^*=(1/18,1/12), rounded b=(5,4) with cost 14, whereas b=(4,4) has cost 12 and sum_j m_j2^(-b_j)=1/4=2 eta. This is a concrete reason not to label the rounded allocation optimal.

For unit x,y,psi, write Vy-psi=V(y-x)+(V-U)x+(Ux-psi). Unitarity and the operator bound imply ||Vy-psi||<=rho+eta+kappa (and the trivial unit-vector cap 2 can be added if desired). All output/work registers remain included.

For r=0 the empty precision sum/cost is zero, the empty allocation is the unique empty choice, and U=V because all gates are unchanged; no division by C is used. This includes the empty gate list. For eta=0 and r>0, the domain delta_j>0 has no feasible point, and no finite bit vector can satisfy this sufficient positive-error budget. Exact access or exact circuit cancellations might still produce zero actual error; infeasibility of this certificate is not impossibility of exact implementation.

A q=0 circuit cannot contain a physical one-qubit rotation, so the nonempty-occurrence case implicitly has q>=1; q=0 is included through the empty parameter case. Supplied interfaces require identical order/types/physical targets. No independence or cancellation assumption is made, no noncommuting gates are reordered, and no spectator dimension factor is introduced.

The optimum is for an explicitly assumed logarithmic supplier cost under a sufficient worst-case certificate. ExactAngle.real and real arithmetic do not furnish effective approximations to arbitrary real inputs. Existence/cost of a certified angle supplier, finite-gate-set compilation, other arithmetic/implementation costs and resource scaling are all separate. This answer proves neither polynomial-time finite-bit synthesis nor optimal physical circuit error.

independent_derivation: Words of length n and coordinate functions x:{0,...,n-1}->{0,1} are in bijection by x(w)_i=w_i; the inverse reads coordinates in increasing wire order. Reversal rho_n is an involution, including n=0.

For a length-n coordinate list z and high appended bit b, L_(n+1)(snoc(z,b))=L_n(z)+2^n b. Reversing x(b::u) yields snoc(rho_n x(u),b). Thus S_(n+1)(b::u)=S_n(u)+2^n b, with S_0(empty)=0. This is precisely M(b::u)=b2^n+M(u), proving S_n=M by induction for all n.

The map L_n is bijective onto {0,...,2^n-1}: at n=0 there is one label/index; recursively L_(n+1)(b::u)=b+2L_n(u), and every integer k<2^(n+1) has unique low bit b=k mod 2 and tail index floor(k/2)<2^n. Composing the word/basis bijection, reversal and L_n proves S_n and hence M are bijective as well. In particular S_n(wordOf(rho_n x))=L_n(rho_n rho_n x)=L_n(x).

For a fixed physical label x, the unique contributing word is wordOf(x). Its amplitude is v_x=F(wordOf(x))=f(M(wordOf(x)))=f(L_n(rho_n x)). The intended coefficient is t_x=f(L_n(x)). Since P|x>=|rho_n x> and rho is its own inverse, (Pv)_x=v_(rho_n x)=f(L_n(x))=t_x.

Without applying P, v=t iff f(L_n(rho_n x))=f(L_n(x)) for every x. Equivalently, define rev_n(k)=L_n(rho_n(L_n^(-1)(k))); the table must satisfy f(rev_n(k))=f(k) at every index, i.e. be constant on reversal orbits. The condition concerns table invariance, not individual word palindromicity.

Because all maps are bijections and coefficients are real, ||v||^2=sum_w F(w)^2=sum_x f(L_n(rho_n x))^2=sum_(k=0)^(2^n-1) f(k)^2=||t||^2=:Q. P is unitary as a basis permutation. If Q>0, normalized vectors v/sqrt(Q) and t/sqrt(Q) obey the same relation P(v/sqrt(Q))=t/sqrt(Q). If Q=0 the table and both vectors are zero and normalization is undefined.

Explicit three-bit discriminator: use the head-first word w=(1,0,0), which is non-palindromic. Its physical low-wire-first label x=(1,0,0) has L_3(x)=1, while M(w)=S_3(w)=4 and L_3(rho_3 x)=4. Take f(k)=1 if k=4 and 0 otherwise. Then v=|physical index 1>, t=|physical index 4>, so the uncorrected vectors are distinct and orthogonal. It satisfies the contraction premise with d_0=d_1=d_2=d_3=1, ell=r=1, A_0(b)=b, A_1(b)=A_2(b)=1-b.

At n=0 there is one empty word, identity contraction, scalar F(empty)=ell r=f(0), and rho=P=identity. At n=1 reversal is also identity, so v=t for every table. Any reversal-invariant table gives v=t for arbitrary n; the zero table gives v=t=0 but no normalized state.

Reversing physical labels changes which bit each already ordered core consumes. It does not replace ell A_0(w_0)...A_(n-1)(w_(n-1))r by the reverse matrix product. The reverse product may even be dimensionally undefined, and when defined generally changes a noncommutative contraction. A mathematical basis relabeling or formula for P does not execute a wire permutation. A real circuit must implement routing/permutation and account for its costs; no SWAP synthesis, free routing, bond cleanup, postselection, or tensor-train preparation algorithm follows from these identities.

Prove the word/basis/index bijections and the public S(wordOf(rho x))=L(x) identity, not merely a three-bit example.
Derive v_x=f(L(rho x)) and transform coefficients with the inverse permutation correctly to get Pv=t.
State necessary and sufficient reversal-invariance of the sample table for uncorrected equality.
